Implement `applyDirectoryCommand(records, command)`, an in-memory command processor. Export exactly `{ applyDirectoryCommand }` using CommonJS. `records` must be an array of non-null objects having a nonempty string `id`, string `label`, and string `contact`; IDs must be unique. `command` must be an object with `type` equal to `"LIST"`, `"GET"`, `"ADD"`, `"UPDATE"`, or `"REMOVE"`. Malformed inputs throw `TypeError`; duplicate IDs throw `RangeError`. `LIST` returns `{ records }` with a new array and shallow copies of all records. `GET` requires string `id` and returns `{ record }`, where `record` is a copy or `null`. `ADD` requires a valid `record`, rejects an existing ID with `RangeError`, and returns `{ records }` containing copies of all old records plus a copy of the new record. `UPDATE` requires string `id` and a non-array object `changes`; it returns `{ records, found }`. If found, merge changes into that record but never allow its `id` to change; if absent, return copied records and `found: false`. `REMOVE` requires string `id` and returns copied remaining records plus `removed`, a copy of the removed record or `null`. Preserve ordering except that additions go last. Neither returned records nor returned arrays may alias inputs, and no operation may mutate its arguments.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
